reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but leaves each consumer to implement the daily skip policy.

duplication.why: The daily skip-versus-shift decision appears in four places, with three additional implementations of the same policy.

placement.why: Holiday classification belongs in shared/schedules.ts, but schedule handlers and budget templates also take responsibility for shared recurrence policy.

scope.why: The changes are focused on the four requested schedule enhancements and their supporting types, tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate four policy implementations and separate occurrence-limit heuristics, while the new handler leaves config untyped despite the existing RecurConfig type.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and createScheduleList decide daily skipping outside applyWeekendRule, bypassing or disabling its adjustment rather than extending the shared policy.

disguised_duplication.where: The same daily non-working-day policy is reshaped into a find predicate in getNextDate, continue branches in the handlers, and isSkippedOccurrence/getShiftedDate closures in createScheduleList.

abstraction_drift.where: A holidays parameter is added to both applyWeekendRule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; their adjustment remains general, but getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and createScheduleList independently implement the daily exception outside those helpers.
